To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) CKD can be employed as a suitable additive in cold bonding pelletization processes for the manufacture of artificial aggregates; (2) the use of CKD in cold bonding processes is an innovative approach that allows the valorization of CKD in the manufacture of artificial light weight aggregates, which in turn, can be used in the production of concrete; (3) the use of cold bonded aggregates in concrete manufacture allows the substitution of natural aggregate, reducing the environmental impact of concrete production; and
cold bonded artificial aggregates were successfully produced using three industrial wastes and that the obtained concretes were suitable for structural applications.
the use of CKD, blast furnace slag and sludge in a cold bonding process for the production of artificial aggregates is a promising way to obtain sustainable and lightweight concrete.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of industrial solid wastes as raw materials in the production of artificial aggregates, and with the use of these aggregates as partial substitutes for the natural aggregates in concrete production.

the production and the use of cold bonded artificial aggregates, which are obtained by pelletizing three different solid wastes (CKD, slag and marble sluge) with a binder (lime) in order to substitute natural coarse aggregates in concrete.
the development of sustainable construction materials, which are obtained from the reuse of solid industrial wastes and which have a positive environmental impact.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cold bonded artificial aggregates are a valid alternative for the substitution of the natural aggregates, and that the use of CKD as an activator of blast furnace slag hydration is a promising strategy for a sustainable and eco-compatible use of industrial solid waste.
the cold bonding pelletisation is a promising process to produce artificial aggregates from industrial wastes, which can be used in the manufacture of lightweight concrete.

the cold bonding pelletisation process is an effective and sustainable way to produce artificial aggregates, and that the addition of CKD in the cold bonding pelletised aggregates is beneficial for the mechanical properties of lightweight concrete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of cold bonding pelletization for the production of artificial aggregates from industrial waste materials is a sustainable and effective solution to reduce the amount of industrial waste and the environmental impact of cement production.
the use of cold bonded artificial aggregates in lightweight concrete production is a promising and sustainable solution for the management of industrial solid wastes.
